title: Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Chemical Reactions Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Chemical processes require energy change as atoms are rearranged: types of reactions (synthesis, decomposition, single and double replacement, combustion), conservation of mass, balancing equations, and exothermic and endothermic reactions. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 10, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 science worksheets (BC): word and skeleton equations, balancing equations, types of reactions, conservation of mass, exothermic and endothermic reactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.
key_sub: Balance an equation by changing coefficients.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a chemical reaction the atoms of the reactants rearrange to form products. The law of conservation of mass says the total mass stays the same, so equations must be balanced by putting coefficients in front of formulas (never changing subscripts).

Types of reactions: synthesis (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), single replacement, double replacement, combustion and neutralization. Exothermic reactions give off heat; endothermic reactions take it in.

Example

Balance: H2 + O2 → H2O

Make the oxygen atoms equal first.

Answer: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O

Example

2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2. What type of reaction is this?

One reactant breaks apart.

Answer: decomposition

Common mistakes

  • Changing subscripts to balance an equation.
  • Thinking mass is lost when a gas is given off (it escapes).
  • Mixing up exothermic and endothermic.

faq.a: Gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) escape into the air.

items.q: How many atoms of H are in H<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Count the subscripts (including any outside parentheses): 2.

items.q: How many atoms of O are in 2CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 2CO<sub>2</sub>: the coefficient 2 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: Benjamin writes this equation for rusting of iron: 5Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. Is it balanced?
c: No. The number of some atoms is different on each side.
Yes, because both sides have the same substances.
items.e: Count each kind of atom on both sides; at least one does not match.

items.q:
Which type of chemical change is shown by this word equation?
nitric acid + calcium hydroxide → calcium nitrate + water
items.e: An acid and an alkali make a salt and water.

items.q: Octane (C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub>) burns completely in oxygen. What are the products?
items.e: Complete combustion of a compound of C and H (and O) gives CO₂ and H₂O.

items.q: Barium reacts with sulfur. What is the formula of the product?
items.e: Barium loses 2 electrons and sulfur gains 2; the charges must cancel.

items.q: Ethan reacts 24 g of carbon with 64 g of oxygen. Both are used up. What mass of carbon dioxide forms?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 24 + 64 = 88 g.

items.q: In Ethan's sealed flask, some hydrogen reacts with 24 g of oxygen and makes 27 g of water. What mass of hydrogen reacted?

items.e: The magnesium gains the mass of the oxygen: 12 + 8.

items.q: Ethan mixes 60 g of one solution with 10 g of another in a sealed flask. A precipitate forms. What is the total mass after the reaction?

items.q: Ethan puts 50 g of marble chips and acid in an open flask. After the reaction it has a mass of 47 g. Why is it lighter?
c: Mass is not conserved in reactions.
Carbon dioxide gas escaped into the air.
items.e: The gas leaves the open flask: 3 g of it.

items.q: Respiration releases energy for the body. Is this exothermic or endothermic?
items.e: Exothermic releases energy (surroundings warm up); endothermic absorbs energy.

items.q: Water is split into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity. What is the sign of the energy change for this change?
items.e: Energy released: the energy change < 0. Energy absorbed: the energy change > 0.
